title: Circuit-breaker-driven traffic tiling and metric signatures for phased experiments
creator: Marco Chen
description: Build a standardized playbook and automation around circuit-breaker style gates, deterministic traffic tiling, and metric signature checks to reduce risk during A/B and canary rollouts. This covers definition of metric signatures, automated gating logic, rollback thresholds, and an ops escalation ladder to keep latency/cost/quality SLOs intact while enabling faster iterative experiments.
milestones: 2026-02-22: Define canonical metric signatures (latency p95, error spike delta, token-cost drift, semantic quality delta)
2026-03-01: Prototype traffic-tiling controller and deterministic sampling library for split tests
2026-03-08: Implement circuit-breaker gate that evaluates windowed metric signatures and triggers automated rollback
2026-03-15: Run internal shadow canary across two product paths and collect SLO telemetry
2026-03-22: Cross-functional review and sign-off; publish experiment-runbook and handover to platform ops
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic traffic-tiling library shipped and integrated in Redwood SDKs for server-side routing
A circuit-breaker gate that can be composed into rollout policies and triggers rollback within 60s of breach
Metric signatures computed and visualized in Console for each experiment with configurable alert thresholds
Runbook with escalation ladder and postmortem template linked from experiment UI
decision_points: Use rolling window size of 5 minutes vs 1 minute for metric signature evaluation (trade-off: sensitivity vs noise)
Expose circuit-breaker as managed policy in Console vs simple API flag (trade-off: discoverability vs complexity)
Default sampling granularity: deterministic hashing by user ID vs session ID for fairness
risks: Over-sensitive gates generate noisy rollbacks for low-volume experiments
Metric drift from model changes may require continuous re-baselining
Integration complexity for Dedicated/private customers with on-prem routing
mitigations: Canary ramp heuristics that increase window size at low volume
Automated baseline re-eval job run weekly for flagged models
Provide a lightweight SDK shim for private deployments to avoid routing changes
updates: 2026-02-18: Scoped initial set of metric signatures with SRE and Applied ML — added token-cost and semantic-quality delta
2026-02-25: Eng spike completed for deterministic tiling; prototype uses xxhash on hashed_id namespace (ENG-29801)
2026-03-03: Design review: Console UIs for gate config accepted with minor copy edits (DES-4122)

review_feedback: SRE: prefer 3-tier severity mapping for gates to avoid immediate full rollback on class-2 degradations
Applied ML: require a semantic-quality holdout eval before opening traffic to >20%
Security: for private deployments, all gate decisions must be exportable to audit logs
notes_for_qa: Simulate low-volume and high-volume traffic profiles to validate gate sensitivity
Introduce synthetic quality regressions (semantic testset) to validate automated rollback
Verify audit log entries include gate decision, timestamp, and triggering metric values
handover: Ops playbook to be published under /runbooks/experiment-gates.md
